technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Cloud Stream binder abstraction for message bus resource cleanup (U1, U2).
Implement stream update via existing deployment lifecycle hooks without full destroy (U3).
Support file-based deployment manifest using YAML/JSON parsing with Spring's resource abstraction (U4).
Use Spring AOP or channel interceptor for adding trace logging per module with wildcard support (U6).
Extend module descriptor to allow side channels via Spring Integration's channel adapters and tap functionality (U7).
Create a standalone Spring Boot application for the NYC taxi trip demo using Spring Cloud Stream (U8).

User stories U5 (reference architectures) and U8 (taxi trip study) are scoped as documentation and a sample application, respectively.

activities.activity_description: Analyze and clarify all eight user stories to finalize acceptance criteria and identify dependencies.
Design the mechanism to automatically clean up message bus queues/topics when a stream is destroyed, handling stale resources.
Write code for resource cleanup logic, including integration with multiple message bus binders, unit tests, and minor integration tests.
Design the ability to modify deployment properties of an existing stream without destroying and recreating it.
Implement the update mechanism, including validation, persistence, and propagation to running stream modules.
Design the parsing and validation of deployment manifest from a file (e.g., YAML, JSON) as an alternative to inline properties.
Implement file resource loading, manifest parsing, and integration with existing deployment controllers.
Create reference architecture documents, diagrams, and sample configuration snippets for common deployment patterns on Spring XD.
Design the optional _trace_ property for streams, including wildcard support (e.g., module.*.trace) and integration with logging notifications.
Implement the trace property parsing, wildcard expansion, and runtime tracing (e.g., using wiretap or log interceptor).
Design the ability to create arbitrary side channels (input/output beyond primary) and tap channels within a module flow.
Implement side channel support, including channel creation, tap configuration, and integration with bus binders.
Develop a complete sample streaming application that processes NYC taxi trip reports to demonstrate event-based analytics.
Perform end-to-end integration tests for all new features across different deployment scenarios.
Write user-facing documentation for all new features (U1–U8) including examples and configuration references.
Conduct self-review and address any issues found during code review, including minor refactoring.
